nodes.name: ImportSite
nodes.documentation:
One import statement and the imported names that capture queries.

`owner` is the module or callable whose scope holds the statement. Each
name range holds bytes in the statement path.

nodes.name: SemanticFact
nodes.documentation: One fact from an LSP server.

nodes.name: EntityEvidence
nodes.documentation:
Source ranges used to match one entity.

Each range holds bytes in the file that `path` names.

```text
def run(value: Request) -> Reply:
    ^^^        ^^^^^^^     ^^^^^
    |          |           +- type_outputs
    |          +- type_inputs
    +- declarations

    return Reply()
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ body
```

`scope` covers the complete definition. A parameter default is outside both
type lists, because it runs in the enclosing scope.

nodes.name: EntityKey
nodes.documentation:
A stable entity identity across builds.

# Grammar

`key = path | key "::" segment`

A segment contains an entity kind, name, and optional sibling ordinal.
Entity kinds are `type`, `callable`, and `field`.

Examples are `pkg/api.py`, `pkg/api.py::type:Router`, and
`pkg/api.py::type:Router::callable:__init__[1]`.

The first sibling of one name keeps no ordinal. A later duplicate does not
change an existing key.

nodes.name: ResolutionFallback
nodes.documentation: Controls symbol matching when no declaration matches.

nodes.name: EdgeAccumulator
nodes.documentation: Edges of one provenance origin, with one edge per source, target, and kind.

nodes.name: SignatureRole
nodes.documentation: Position of a type in a callable signature.

nodes.name: LanguageAdapter
nodes.documentation:
What one language must report to produce a graph.

An adapter selects its sources and reads its syntax. It returns facts only.
`graph::build` turns them into a graph, and `resolve` asks the language
server of the profile for semantic edges.

nodes.name: CallableAnnotations
nodes.documentation: The signature annotation ranges of one callable.

nodes.name: Scope
nodes.documentation: One lexical owner of declarations.

nodes.name: CallableSyntax
nodes.documentation: The parts of one callable that its facts read.

nodes.name: Binding
nodes.documentation: The variable declaration that the walker is in.

nodes.name: BoundFunction
nodes.documentation: A function that a variable or a class property names.

nodes.name: Member
nodes.documentation: One function or method in a list of siblings.

nodes.name: Group
nodes.documentation: The declarations and source extent of one overload group.

nodes.name: Overloads
nodes.documentation: The overload groups of one document, by the scope start of each member.

nodes.name: Batch
nodes.documentation: Requests that the client sends together, with the label of each.

nodes.name: BatchResults
nodes.documentation: The raw results of one batch, decoded group by group in input order.

nodes.name: DocumentIndex
nodes.documentation: The URI and text of each open document by source path.

nodes.name: InFlight
nodes.documentation: One batch request that waits for its answer.

nodes.name: FakeServer
nodes.documentation:
One compiled fake server in its own folder.

Each test compiles its own server, because the program writes its
shutdown marker next to its executable.

nodes.name: SemanticCapture
nodes.documentation: Preserves protocol values, response grouping, and fact order until normalization.

nodes.name: CapturedDocument
nodes.documentation:
The relative path identifies the document, exactly as it does in a source
snapshot. Normalization joins the two on that path.

nodes.name: ProtocolSymbolSite
nodes.documentation:
A protocol symbol site that later becomes a `SymbolAnchor`.

The selection covers the declared name.

nodes.name: CapturedSemanticFact
nodes.documentation: The vectors preserve each grouped protocol response.

nodes.name: SourceLookup
nodes.documentation:
Finds the selected source that one protocol URI names.

The lookup first matches exact URI text. After a miss, it converts the URI
to a path and matches that path.

nodes.name: ServerReadiness
nodes.documentation: States when a server answers semantic requests correctly.

nodes.name: Indexed
nodes.documentation: A graph and the hash of the source files that it was built from.

nodes.name: Parsed
nodes.documentation: One parsed codebase: the input and output of `run`, with the import sites of each language.

nodes.name: Resolver
nodes.documentation:
One parsed codebase and the language servers that resolve its node keys.

A server starts at the first key of its language and stays until `shutdown`.

nodes.name: Session
nodes.documentation: One running language server and the documents it has open.

nodes.name: Scope
nodes.documentation: The parsed sources of one language during one resolution.

nodes.name: DocumentSnapshot
nodes.documentation: The relative path identifies the document across analysis stages.

nodes.name: SourceRange
nodes.documentation:
A half-open UTF-8 byte range.

`start` belongs to the range. `end` does not belong to the range.

nodes.name: ContentHash
nodes.documentation:
Identifies the text of one source range.

The value is a 64-bit FNV-1a hash defined here, so it stays identical on
every machine and every toolchain.

nodes.name: ArtifactIndex
nodes.documentation: The catalog document of one store.

nodes.name: ArtifactIndexEntry
nodes.documentation:
One graph file. `digest` names the merged graph document that `serve`
sends, and `graph_digest` names the bytes of the graph file, as flows bind
them. The two differ when the semantic cache adds edges.

nodes.name: FlowListing
nodes.documentation:
One flow listing. `file` is relative to `flows/`.

A flow is stale when its bound graph file is missing or its byte digest
differs from the bound digest.

nodes.name: LineageListing
nodes.documentation: The current generation of one flow and the graph binding that decides its freshness.

nodes.name: ServerCheck
nodes.documentation: The check of one language server.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.documentation: The state of one server. `Broken` and `Missing` fail the check.

nodes.name: Probe
nodes.documentation: The result of one version command.

nodes.name: Nodes
nodes.documentation: The nodes of a `show` with several keys, in key order.

nodes.name: InGraph
nodes.documentation: One query result with the graph file that answered it.

nodes.name: Destination
nodes.documentation:
The root to analyze, the graph file to write, and the store and file name when it is indexed.

`create_store` is true when the destination is a new project store.
`project_root` is true when index analyzes the project root instead of the working directory.

nodes.name: DiffIssue
nodes.documentation: One problem of an agent document or of a derivation. `path` is a JSON pointer.

nodes.name: Prepared
nodes.documentation: The checked-out and indexed base of one diff.

nodes.name: ImportRequest
nodes.documentation: One import request. `author` comes from the invocation, never from the agent.

nodes.name: FrozenDiff
nodes.documentation: The result of one successful freeze.

nodes.name: VerifyReport
nodes.documentation: The result of one verify.

nodes.name: DiffListing
nodes.documentation: One frozen diff in a listing.

nodes.name: AgentDiff
nodes.documentation: The only data that a coding agent writes for one diff.

nodes.name: AgentPair
nodes.documentation: One Before step and one After step that are the same step. Numbers count from 1 in flow order.

nodes.name: DiffArtifact
nodes.documentation: One frozen diff. `digest` covers every field except `digest` and `provenance`.

nodes.name: DiffSide
nodes.documentation: One side of the diff: a full commit ID and the frozen flow on that commit.

nodes.name: DiffRow
nodes.documentation:
The derived facts of one step, or of one pair of steps.

`base_span` and `head_span` locate the function on each commit. A new step
compares with the function of the same node key on the base, when it exists;
a removed step compares with the function on the head.

nodes.name: ChangeKind
nodes.documentation: `moved` means that the function is in another file. A cluster change is never a move.

nodes.name: LineSpan
nodes.documentation: Lines `start` to `end` of one file, counted from 1, both included.

nodes.name: Change
nodes.documentation: One item of a keyed walk. `item` is a current item, or a removed base item.

nodes.name: GenerationBody
nodes.documentation: The artifact without digests and provenance: the input of the generation digest.

nodes.name: CallGraph
nodes.documentation: Static `calls` edges between fact nodes.

nodes.name: ImportRequest
nodes.documentation: One import request. `author` comes from the invocation, never from the agent.

nodes.name: FrozenGeneration
nodes.documentation: The result of one successful freeze.

nodes.name: CurrentPointer
nodes.documentation: Names the current generation of one flow.

nodes.name: StoredGeneration
nodes.documentation: One stored generation and its path relative to `flows/`.

nodes.name: AgentStep
nodes.documentation: `prior_step_id` and `node_key` are references only; the agent never mints IDs.

nodes.name: GenerationPurpose
nodes.documentation: `initial` starts a lineage. `revision` changes the intent on the same graph.

nodes.name: InputCategory
nodes.documentation: The assignment inputs that differ from the parent.

nodes.name: StepDiff
nodes.documentation: `changed_fields` is empty unless the step is retained.

nodes.name: ClusterDiff
nodes.documentation: `changed_fields` is empty unless the cluster is retained.

nodes.name: MemberDiff
nodes.documentation: `causes` names the input categories that differ among the inputs of this node's decisions.

nodes.name: FactBinding
nodes.documentation: `graph_digest` is the SHA-256 of the exact graph bytes. It is excluded from the facts digest.

nodes.name: ClusterIntent
nodes.documentation:
`phase_note` is present if and only if `phase` is `Other`.

`input` and `output` name the data models that enter and leave the group. An
empty list means that no data model enters or leaves it.

nodes.name: FlowStep
nodes.documentation: `attested_fact_digest` is the node fact digest at the last agent write of this step.

nodes.name: StepLedger
nodes.documentation:
The step text: one row for each slot that the step uses.

A null slot is not used. A used slot holds one or more one-line items, and at
least one slot is used. Items name identifiers with marks such as
`` `fn:read_graph` ``.

nodes.name: FlowIssue
nodes.documentation: One problem with an agent output or a stored artifact. `path` is a JSON pointer.

nodes.name: ClusterColor
nodes.documentation: Palette slots in order. A new cluster takes the lowest free slot.

nodes.name: Transition
nodes.documentation: The static call relation from the previous step node. Not a runtime observation.

nodes.name: PriorContext
nodes.documentation: The prior version that an agent output may continue.

nodes.name: CheckedStep
nodes.documentation: One agent step after canonicalization and reference checks.

nodes.name: CheckedFlow
nodes.documentation: One agent flow after canonicalization and reference checks.

nodes.name: StepReferences
nodes.documentation: The references that one agent step may name.

nodes.name: TextRule
nodes.documentation:
The length limits of one text field. A `block` text can hold tabs and line feeds.

A test compares each limit with the JSON Schemas.

nodes.name: VerifyReport
nodes.documentation: The result of one verification. `issues` is empty for a valid generation.

nodes.name: NodeSummary
nodes.documentation: One node in a search result.

nodes.name: SearchResult
nodes.documentation: The ranked matches of one search. `total` counts the matches before the limit.

nodes.name: NodeRef
nodes.documentation: One node reference in a neighbor list.

nodes.name: NodeDetail
nodes.documentation:
One node with its declaration facts and its static neighbors.

`callers` and `callees` come from `calls` edges only. `container` and
`members` come from `contains` edges.

nodes.name: Request
nodes.documentation: One request line.

nodes.name: Response
nodes.documentation: One answer line: `{"ok": true}` or `{"error": "..."}`.

nodes.name: Daemon
nodes.documentation:
The state of one daemon: its store, its project, its profiles, and the warm resolver.

`exit` is true after an answer that another daemon must serve the next request.

nodes.name: ViewerServer
nodes.documentation: One viewer server bound to `127.0.0.1`.

nodes.name: Reply
nodes.documentation: One response before it goes on the wire.

nodes.name: SourceDocument
nodes.documentation: The source of every distinct step function of one flow.

nodes.name: FunctionSource
nodes.documentation: The source of one step function, or why it has none.

nodes.name: SourceCut
nodes.documentation: The lines of one function. Line numbers are one-based.

nodes.name: CutError
nodes.documentation: Why one node cannot be cut from its file text.

nodes.name: Lines
nodes.documentation: The line starts of one text.

nodes.name: ArtifactNode
nodes.documentation:
`id` identifies this node inside this document. `key` preserves the entity
key supplied by the graph.

`kind` selects callable, field, or type metadata. Serde omits absent metadata.

nodes.name: ArtifactEdge
nodes.documentation: `weight` and `observations` preserve the graph edge values.

nodes.name: ArtifactRange
nodes.documentation: One half-open UTF-8 byte range.

nodes.name: NodeKind
nodes.documentation: The kind of one graph node. Serde refuses any other value on read.

nodes.name: RelationKind
nodes.documentation: The kind of one graph edge. Serde refuses any other value on read.

nodes.name: Origin
nodes.documentation: The analysis stage that made one node or edge. Serde refuses any other value on read.

nodes.name: OpenFailure
nodes.documentation: Why `open_regular` cannot open a file.

nodes.name: SemanticCache
nodes.documentation:
The resolved node keys of one graph file and the semantic edges that touch them.

A key is resolved when its callers, its outgoing calls, the uses of it, the
types of its locals, and the imports of it and of its file are in `edges`.
Some edges of a key appear once their other end is resolved too: its own
signature types (until then a parameter type is a `uses_type` edge), the
values and fields that it uses, and calls in macros, function values, or
module-level code. Keys and edges are sorted, and one source, target, and
kind has one edge.

nodes.documentation: One semantic edge between two node keys.

    kind: Option<NodeKind>,
    limit: usize,

nodes.documentation:
Returns the nodes whose key contains every word of `text`, best match first.

Matching ignores case. Spaces, `::`, `:`, `.`, and `/` separate words, so a
qualified name such as `Command::parse` or a path such as `flow/import`
works. The name decides the rank: the exact name, then a name that starts
with the first word and holds every word, then a name that holds every
word, then a name that holds some words, then a key match only. The exact
name is the words joined with `_`; for a qualified or path query it is the
last word. A file module ranks by its file stem, not by its path. Nodes in
tests come after all other nodes. In each rank, callables come before
types, modules, and fields; the key breaks ties.

nodes.name: write_cache
nodes.signature: pub fn write_cache(directory: &Path, graph_file: &str, cache: &SemanticCache) -> io::Result<()>
nodes.documentation:
Adds the resolved keys and the edges of `cache` to the stored cache of one graph file.

The write holds the store lock and replaces the file atomically. The stored
keys and edges of the same digest stay. Two edges with the same source,
target, and kind merge into one with the larger weight, and a type use that
a signature edge states goes, as the graph semantic stage drops it. So the
stored cache does not depend on the order or the grouping of resolutions.

# Errors

Returns `InvalidInput` if the digest of the graph file is not
`cache.graph_digest`, so edges of an older graph never replace a newer cache.
Returns an error for an invalid graph name, a link, or a failed read or write.

A cached edge with the source, target, and kind of a graph edge sets the
weight of that edge. The other cached edges follow the graph edges, with a
semantic origin and no observations. A cached edge that names a key outside
the graph is skipped.

Returns an error if the graph or its cache cannot be read.

and not parsed. `serve` sends this document for the graph file.

Returns an error if the graph or its cache cannot be read.
